Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns preparation, BMA submission and sign-off of the annual statutory financial return and BSCR/EBS schedules for each licensed Bermuda entity; escalates to CFO on any filing-readiness risk.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Insurance Act 1978, ss.17-18 (statutory financial return) and the Insurance (Prudential Standards) (Class 4 and Class 3B Solvency Requirement) Rules 2008 (BSCR), re-read against the current BMA Statutory Reporting Guidance Notes at each filing cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Year-end close, statutory financial statement preparation, BSCR calculation, GAAP/EBS reconciliation and BMA electronic submission, for every Bermuda-licensed (re)insurance entity in the group (Class 3A/3B/4).

In-scope systems.value: General ledger trial balance feeding statutory statements; BSCR built on the actuarial modeling platform; filed through the BMA's online statutory filing portal.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Bermuda Statutory Return & BSCR Filing Procedure - close calendar, data extraction, BSCR build, EBS reconciliation, auditor sign-off, BMA portal submission and evidence retention.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer; reviewed annually and whenever the BMA revises the Statutory Reporting Guidance Notes or BSCR rules.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Statutory financial return and BSCR due within four months of financial year-end (extendable to six months on written BMA approval); tracked on the group regulatory filing calendar by legal entity.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at FYE+60/FYE+90/FYE+110 days to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and CFO for each in-scope entity.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed statutory statements, BSCR workpapers, auditor opinion and BMA submission confirmation retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed or late filing logged as a compliance exception with root cause, BMA notification record and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off any late-filing remediation and any BMA extension request before submission.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All Bermuda-licensed entities' statutory financial returns and BSCR filings due in the year, drawn from the group regulatory filing calendar.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a filing missing its BMA deadline (including any approved extension); any capital ratio miscalculation greater than 1% of ECR/MSM is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per entity; test performed annually over the full population of Bermuda filings for the year.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the preparers of the statutory statements and BSCR schedules.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual BMA filing test workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to each entity's submission confirmation.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed statutory return, BSCR schedules, audited GAAP statements and BMA acknowledgment, assembled within 5 business days of a BMA request.

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager coordinates the BMA response; CFO clears any substantive answer before it is sent.

checklist.step: Confirm the entity population and filing class for the year
actions: Pull the group entity register and licensing schedule from Corporate Secretary to identify every Bermuda-licensed entity and its class (3A/3B/4/C/D/E).
Confirm the financial year-end date per entity.
Note any entity that changed class or was newly registered during the year and flag its first filing.
Record the population on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the filing tracker lists every in-scope entity, class and FYE with no omissions confirmed against the licensing schedule.

checklist.step: Build the close calendar and lock the data cut-off
actions: Work with Controller to set the statutory close calendar keyed to FYE+4 months.
Confirm the GL trial balance freeze date in the ERP.
Distribute the calendar to Controller, Appointed Actuary and Capital Model Actuary.
Load milestone dates into the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the close calendar is issued with a GL freeze date and BSCR build date that both land before the statutory deadline.

checklist.step: Extract the statutory trial balance and prepare statutory financial statements
actions: In the ERP General Ledger module run the trial balance report for the statutory entity and period.
Map GL accounts to the BMA statutory statement line items using the entity's chart-of-accounts mapping.
Prepare the statutory balance sheet, statement of income and capital statement.
Reconcile the statutory net income to management accounts and document any adjustment.
checklist.done: the statutory financial statements tie to the GL trial balance and all adjustments are documented and explained.

checklist.step: Build the BSCR (or applicable solvency) schedule
actions: Load current-year balance sheet and underwriting data into the BSCR model.
Run the fixed-income, credit, underwriting and operational risk charges per the current BSCR rules.
Compute the Enhanced Capital Requirement (ECR) and compare it to statutory capital and surplus.
Version and save the model run with the entity and period in the filename.
checklist.done: the BSCR/ECR calculation is complete, versioned and reconciled to the statutory balance sheet.

checklist.step: Prepare the Economic Balance Sheet (EBS) reconciliation where the entity is subject to EBS reporting
actions: Reconcile the GAAP/statutory balance sheet to the EBS basis (fair value adjustments, technical provisions on a best-estimate plus risk margin basis).
Document each reconciling item with its methodology.
Route to the Appointed Actuary for review of technical provision assumptions.
checklist.done: the EBS reconciliation is fully itemized and reviewed by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Obtain the Appointed Actuary's statutory opinion
actions: Review loss reserves, technical provisions and the EBS best-estimate liability for reasonableness.
Sign the Statement of Actuarial Opinion required with the statutory filing.
Note any qualification or scope limitation in writing.
Deliver the signed opinion to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: a signed, unqualified (or clearly qualified) Statement of Actuarial Opinion is on file ahead of the filing deadline.

checklist.step: Route statutory statements and BSCR for external audit
actions: Deliver the statutory financial statements, BSCR workpapers and supporting schedules to the BMA-approved external auditor.
Respond to audit queries within the agreed turnaround.
Track open items on the audit PBC (prepared-by-client) list.
checklist.done: the auditor has all requested schedules and the PBC list shows no open items past its due date.

checklist.step: Obtain the audit opinion and resolve any adjustments
actions: Receive the auditor's opinion on the statutory financial statements (and GAAP statements for commercial insurers).
Post any audit adjustment to the GL and re-run the affected statutory statements and BSCR.
Confirm the final numbers agree between the audited statements and the BSCR filing.
checklist.done: the audited statutory statements and BSCR figures agree with no unresolved audit adjustments.

checklist.step: Complete the Declaration of Compliance and other statutory certificates
actions: Complete the Declaration of Compliance confirming the entity met minimum criteria and prudential requirements throughout the year.
Obtain director certification per the Insurance Act requirements.
Attach supporting schedules referenced in the declaration.
checklist.done: the Declaration of Compliance is completed and certified by an authorized director.

checklist.step: Obtain board or board-committee approval of the statutory package
actions: Upload the statutory financial statements, BSCR summary, actuarial opinion and Declaration of Compliance to the board portal ahead of the approval meeting.
Present capital adequacy results (ECR/MSM ratios) to the board or Risk Committee.
Record the board's approval and any conditions in the minutes.
checklist.done: board or committee minutes show approval of the statutory package before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the filing through the BMA's statutory filing channel
actions: Log in to the BMA's online statutory filing system with the entity's filer credentials.
Upload the audited statutory financial statements, BSCR/EBS schedules, actuarial opinion and Declaration of Compliance in the required file formats.
Complete any online data-entry schedules the portal requires.
Submit and retain the system-generated submission confirmation and reference number.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted through the BMA portal and a dated confirmation with reference number is on file.

checklist.step: Track solvency ratio results against internal escalation thresholds
actions: Compare the filed ECR and MSM coverage ratios to the entity's internal target and regulatory minimum.
Where a ratio falls within 25 percentage points of the regulatory minimum, open a capital management escalation.
Notify the Head of Capital Management and CFO.
checklist.done: solvency ratio results are compared to thresholds and any near-breach is escalated in writing.

checklist.step: File and index the submission package
actions: Save the final statutory statements, BSCR workpapers, actuarial opinion, Declaration of Compliance and BMA confirmation into the compliance evidence repository under the entity and financial year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the index is searchable by entity and filing year.
checklist.done: the complete submission package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

checklist.step: Log any late or incomplete filing as an exception
actions: Where a deadline is missed or an extension is needed, open a tracker exception recording the cause, BMA correspondence and revised date.
Notify the CFO and Regulatory Counsel.
Request any extension in writing before the original deadline lapses.
checklist.done: any missed deadline is logged with cause, correspondence and CFO notification before or at the deadline.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with CFO sign-off and carry lessons into next year's calendar
actions: Review the completed filing package and any exceptions raised during the cycle.
Sign off the cycle as closed.
Update the close calendar and procedure for next year with any timing or data issues found.
checklist.done: CFO sign-off is recorded and the next cycle's close calendar reflects this year's lessons learned.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory filings due in the year
actions: Pull the group entity register and filing tracker to list every Bermuda-licensed entity with a statutory filing due in the test period.
Reconcile the count to the prior year's population plus any new registrations or exits.
Resolve discrepancies before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the entity register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filing tracker to BMA submission confirmations
actions: For each entity in the population, match the filing tracker's submitted date to the BMA portal confirmation reference and date.
List any entity with no confirmation on file as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population entity is matched to a BMA confirmation or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the test sample
actions: Take 100% of Class 4 entities and any entity that missed a prior-year deadline.
Take a random sample of remaining entities, minimum 5, or 100% if the population is under 10.
Record the seed and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all Class 4 entities.

testing.step: Re-perform the BSCR calculation independently for sampled entities
actions: Rebuild the ECR/BSCR calculation from the audited statutory balance sheet independently of the original model run.
Compare the recomputed ECR and ratio to the filed figure.
Treat any difference beyond model rounding tolerance as an exception.
testing.done: the recomputed BSCR/ECR for each sampled entity agrees with the filed figure or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the audit opinion and Appointed Actuary opinion are genuine and unqualified where claimed
actions: Obtain the signed audit opinion and Statement of Actuarial Opinion directly from the auditor's and actuary's files.
Confirm signature, date and scope match what was filed.
Flag any qualification not disclosed in the filing package.
testing.done: the audit and actuarial opinions are verified as authentic and any qualification is confirmed as disclosed.

testing.step: Trace the filing to the BMA portal confirmation and check submission timing
actions: Log evidence of the BMA portal confirmation screen or downloaded receipt for each sampled entity.
Compare the submission timestamp to the statutory deadline (FYE+4 months or approved extension).
Note any late submission.
testing.done: each sampled filing traces to a BMA confirmation submitted on or before its deadline.

testing.step: Confirm board approval pre-dates submission
actions: Pull board or committee minutes for each sampled entity's statutory package approval.
Confirm the approval date is before the BMA submission date.
Flag any filing submitted before board approval.
testing.done: board approval pre-dates submission for every sampled entity or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Recompute solvency ratio escalation thresholds
actions: For sampled entities, recompute the ECR/MSM coverage ratio and compare to the internal 25-point escalation threshold.
Confirm any near-breach was escalated per the checklist.
Note any missed escalation.
testing.done: the escalation logic is independently confirmed for every sampled entity with a near-breach ratio.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found (late filing, unreconciled BSCR, missing approval).
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled work sign the workpaper.
Report results and any open breaches to the Audit or Risk Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual CISSA process end to end - scoping, risk identification, capital assessment and board presentation - for each Bermuda commercial insurer required to file.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Insurance (Prudential Standards) (Class 4 and Class 3B Solvency Requirement) Rules 2008 (CISSA requirement), re-read against the current BMA CISSA Guidance Notes each cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Enterprise risk identification, capital adequacy assessment over the business planning horizon, stress and scenario testing, board review, and CISSA report finalization and BMA submission, for each Class 4/3B (and applicable Class 3A/C/D/E) entity.

In-scope systems.value: Own-risk capital model built on the actuarial modeling platform; risk register maintained in the GRC platform; CISSA report drafted and stored in the compliance evidence repository.

Compliance procedure documented.value: CISSA Preparation Procedure - risk universe review, own capital assessment methodology, stress testing linkage, board review cadence and BMA submission steps.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and Board Risk Committee; reviewed annually and on any material change to the risk profile or business plan.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: CISSA filed with the annual statutory return, within four months of financial year-end (or the BMA-approved extension); tracked on the group regulatory filing calendar.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at FYE+60/FYE+90 days to the Chief Risk Officer and Board Risk Committee chair ahead of the CISSA deadline.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Board-approved CISSA report, own capital model output and Risk Committee minutes retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed CISSA deadline or a CISSA filed without board approval is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation owner.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs off any remediation of a late or incomplete CISSA submission.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The CISSA report and supporting own capital model filed for each in-scope Bermuda entity in the year.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if the filed CISSA lacks documented board approval pre-dating submission, or if the own capital assessment does not cover the full business planning horizon (typically 3 years forward).

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test performed annually over 100% of in-scope entities given the low population count.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the risk team that authored the CISSA.

Evidence location for test results.value: CISSA test workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the board minutes and BMA submission confirmation.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Board-approved CISSA report, own capital model summary and BMA submission confirmation, assembled within 5 business days of a BMA request.

Regulator response path.value: Chief Risk Officer coordinates the BMA response on CISSA content; Regulatory Counsel clears any substantive answer.

checklist.step: Confirm the entities required to file a CISSA
actions: Check the licensing class of each Bermuda entity against the CISSA applicability thresholds in the Solvency Requirement Rules.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel any entity newly crossing the threshold.
Record the in-scope list on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the filing tracker lists every entity required to file a CISSA for the year, confirmed against class and thresholds.

checklist.step: Set the CISSA planning horizon and scope
actions: Confirm the business planning horizon (typically 3 years) from the approved business plan.
Agree the risk universe to be assessed (underwriting, market, credit, liquidity, operational, group, emerging) with the Board Risk Committee.
Document scope in the CISSA workplan.
checklist.done: the workplan states the planning horizon and risk universe, agreed with the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Update the enterprise risk register
actions: In the GRC platform review and refresh the risk register for the entity, adding any new or emerging risk identified since the prior CISSA.
Score each risk's likelihood and impact.
Link each material risk to the capital or scenario analysis that addresses it.
checklist.done: the risk register is current, scored and each material risk is linked to the CISSA capital assessment.

checklist.step: Build the own capital assessment model run
actions: Project the balance sheet and capital position over the planning horizon under the base business plan.
Run the own-risk capital calculation reflecting the entity's actual risk profile (beyond the standard BSCR formula where risks are entity-specific).
Document all methodology and assumption changes from the prior year.
checklist.done: the own capital projection covers the full planning horizon with documented methodology and assumptions.

checklist.step: Run the required stress and scenario tests feeding the CISSA
actions: Run the BMA-mandated and internally-defined stress scenarios (reserve deterioration, catastrophe accumulation, market shock, reinsurer default) against the projected balance sheet.
Compute post-stress capital ratios for each scenario.
Identify any scenario breaching the internal capital target or regulatory minimum.
checklist.done: all required stress scenarios are run with post-stress capital ratios computed and any breach identified.

checklist.step: Assess capital management actions and contingency plans
actions: For any scenario showing a capital shortfall, document available management actions (capital injection, reinsurance, business mix change) and their expected impact and lead time.
Confirm actions are realistic given the entity's actual capital-raising history.
checklist.done: every capital shortfall scenario has a documented, credible management action and lead time.

checklist.step: Draft the CISSA report
actions: Draft the CISSA report per the BMA's prescribed structure: risk profile, own capital assessment methodology, stress and scenario results, capital management actions, governance framework.
Incorporate the risk register and capital model outputs.
Circulate to Chief Risk Officer for technical review.
checklist.done: the draft CISSA report is complete against the BMA's required structure and technically reviewed.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary review of the technical provisions and capital methodology
actions: Review the reserving and capital methodology underlying the own capital assessment for consistency with the statutory actuarial opinion.
Confirm assumptions used in CISSA stress tests are consistent with the year-end reserving basis.
Sign off the technical sections.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary sign-off is recorded on the CISSA's technical provisions and capital methodology sections.

checklist.step: Present the draft CISSA to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the draft CISSA report and executive summary to the board portal ahead of the Risk Committee meeting.
Present the risk profile, capital assessment results and any capital shortfall scenarios.
Capture committee questions and required revisions.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee meeting record shows the draft CISSA was presented with questions and revisions captured.

checklist.step: Incorporate committee feedback and finalize the report
actions: Revise the CISSA report to address Risk Committee feedback.
Re-circulate to Chief Risk Officer and Appointed Actuary for final sign-off.
Version and date the final report.
checklist.done: the final CISSA report incorporates committee feedback and carries CRO and Appointed Actuary sign-off.

checklist.step: Obtain full board approval
actions: Place the final CISSA report on the board (or delegated committee) agenda for formal approval.
Record the approval resolution in the board minutes.
Obtain the required director signatures or electronic approval in the board portal.
checklist.done: board minutes record formal approval of the final CISSA report with the approval date.

checklist.step: Submit the CISSA through the BMA filing channel
actions: Log in to the BMA's online statutory filing system.
Upload the board-approved CISSA report in the required format alongside the statutory financial return.
Retain the system-generated submission confirmation.
checklist.done: the CISSA is submitted through the BMA portal with a dated confirmation on file.

checklist.step: File and index the CISSA package
actions: Save the final CISSA report, risk register extract, capital model output, Risk Committee minutes and board approval into the compliance evidence repository under the entity and year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the complete CISSA package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

checklist.step: Log any CISSA delay or scope gap as an exception
actions: Where the CISSA is at risk of missing the filing deadline or a required risk area was not assessed, open a tracker exception with cause and remediation plan.
Notify the Board Risk Committee chair.
checklist.done: any delay or scope gap is logged with cause, remediation plan and committee notification.

checklist.step: Carry capital management actions into the business plan
actions: Feed any capital management action identified in the CISSA into the next annual business planning cycle.
Confirm with Head of Capital Management that action owners and timelines are reflected in the plan.
checklist.done: the business plan for the following year reflects the CISSA's capital management actions with owners and timelines.

testing.step: Build the population of CISSA filings due in the year
actions: Pull the filing tracker for every entity required to file a CISSA in the test period.
Reconcile to the licensing class list.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the licensing class list and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile filings to BMA submission confirmations
actions: Match each population entity's CISSA to its BMA portal confirmation date.
List any entity with no confirmation as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population entity is matched to a confirmation or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of the population given the typically small number of in-scope entities, or a minimum of 5 entities where the population exceeds 10.
Record the selection basis and date.
testing.done: the sample selection is documented and reproducible.

testing.step: Confirm the risk register underlying the CISSA was current
actions: Pull the risk register as of the CISSA drafting date for each sampled entity.
Compare to the version referenced in the CISSA report.
Flag any material risk missing from the report.
testing.done: the risk register version is confirmed current and complete for each sampled CISSA.

testing.step: Re-perform key stress scenario calculations
actions: Independently rerun at least one material stress scenario per sampled entity from the same starting balance sheet and assumptions.
Compare the resulting post-stress capital ratio to the filed CISSA figure.
Treat material differences as exceptions.
testing.done: the independently rerun stress results agree with the filed CISSA or differences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Verify Appointed Actuary sign-off on technical sections
actions: Obtain the signed technical review from the Appointed Actuary's files for each sampled entity.
Confirm date and scope match what is referenced in the CISSA report.
testing.done: the Appointed Actuary sign-off is verified as authentic and appropriately scoped for each sampled entity.

testing.step: Confirm board approval pre-dates BMA submission
actions: Pull board or Risk Committee minutes for each sampled entity.
Confirm the approval date is before the BMA submission date.
Flag any filing submitted before approval.
testing.done: board approval pre-dates submission for every sampled entity or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Test capital management action credibility
actions: For sampled entities with a documented capital shortfall scenario, confirm the stated management action was actually available (e.g. check capital facility agreements or reinsurance treaty terms) at the assessment date.
Flag any action that was not genuinely available.
testing.done: capital management actions are confirmed credible and available, or the gap is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual stress and scenario testing program (BSCR/CISSA-linked, catastrophe and reverse stress scenarios) and the resulting test-results register for each in-scope Bermuda entity.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Insurance (Prudential Standards) (Class 4 and Class 3B Solvency Requirement) Rules 2008 stress/scenario provisions, re-read against current BMA guidance on group and entity stress testing each cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Scenario design, model execution, capital impact assessment, results review and sign-off, and feed into CISSA and BSCR capital add-ons, for each Class 4/3B (and applicable Class 3A/C/D/E) entity.

In-scope systems.value: Base and stressed balance sheets run on the actuarial modeling platform; catastrophe scenarios run through the group's catastrophe modeling tool; results logged in a stress-test results register.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Stress and Scenario Testing Procedure - scenario library, severity calibration, model execution steps, results review and escalation thresholds.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer; reviewed annually and whenever the BMA issues a new mandated scenario or the risk profile changes materially.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Stress and scenario test results finalized ahead of the CISSA board presentation, within four months of financial year-end; any ad hoc BMA-requested stress test completed within the timeframe the BMA specifies in its request letter.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Test-results register milestone alerts at FYE+45/FYE+75 days to the Chief Risk Officer, ahead of the CISSA board presentation deadline.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Stress-test results register, model run outputs and sign-off retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any scenario not run, or a breach not escalated per threshold, is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs off remediation of any missed scenario or unescalated capital breach.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All mandated and internally-defined stress and scenario runs completed in the year for each in-scope entity, per the stress-test results register.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a required scenario (BMA-mandated or internally defined material risk) was not run, or if a breach of the internal capital trigger was not escalated within the procedure's timeframe.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test performed annually over 100% of the mandated scenarios plus a sample of internally-defined scenarios.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the actuary who built and ran the stress scenarios.

Evidence location for test results.value: Stress-test verification workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the model run outputs and CISSA report.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Stress-test results register, scenario methodology notes and escalation log, assembled within 5 business days of a BMA request.

Regulator response path.value: Chief Risk Officer coordinates the BMA response on stress-testing methodology and results; Appointed Actuary supports on technical assumptions.

checklist.step: Confirm the mandated and internally-required scenario set for the year
actions: Review the current BMA guidance and any entity-specific BMA request letter for mandated scenarios.
Add internally-defined scenarios covering the entity's top risks from the risk register.
Compile the scenario list with severity levels on the stress-test workplan.
checklist.done: the workplan lists every mandated and internally-required scenario with its severity level.

checklist.step: Set the base balance sheet and assumptions
actions: Confirm the base (unstressed) balance sheet date and figures agree with the latest reserving and finance close.
Lock the base assumptions (mortality/morbidity, loss ratios, investment returns, expenses) used across all scenarios.
Document the base case in the model.
checklist.done: the base balance sheet and assumptions are locked, documented and agreed to the latest close.

checklist.step: Calibrate each scenario's severity
actions: For market scenarios set the shock parameters (equity, interest rate, credit spread, FX moves) against the BMA-prescribed or internally calibrated severities.
For underwriting scenarios set loss ratio deterioration or reserve strengthening percentages.
Document the calibration source for each parameter.
checklist.done: every scenario has documented, sourced severity parameters.

checklist.step: Run catastrophe accumulation scenarios where the entity writes property/cat risk
actions: Load the current in-force exposure data into the catastrophe model.
Run the required return-period events (e.g. 1-in-100, 1-in-250 year) for the entity's peak zones.
Extract the modeled loss and reinsurance recovery for each event.
checklist.done: catastrophe scenarios are run for all peak zones with modeled loss and net recovery extracted.

checklist.step: Execute the stressed balance sheet runs
actions: Apply each calibrated scenario to the base balance sheet in the actuarial modeling platform.
Compute the post-stress capital and surplus position and the resulting ECR/BSCR ratio for each scenario.
Save each run with a unique scenario identifier.
checklist.done: every scenario in the workplan has a saved, uniquely identified stressed balance sheet run.

checklist.step: Compute reverse stress test breakpoints
actions: Identify the combination of loss/market movements that would breach the entity's minimum solvency margin.
Document the implied scenario and its plausibility assessment.
checklist.done: the reverse stress breakpoint and its plausibility assessment are documented.

checklist.step: Assess each scenario result against the internal capital trigger
actions: Compare each scenario's post-stress ratio to the internal capital management trigger (set above the regulatory minimum).
Mark any scenario breaching the trigger for escalation.
Note the margin to breach for scenarios close to the trigger.
checklist.done: every scenario result is assessed against the trigger with breaches clearly marked.

checklist.step: Escalate trigger breaches to the Board Risk Committee
actions: For any breaching scenario, prepare an escalation memo describing the scenario, the capital shortfall and available management actions.
Present to the Board Risk Committee at its next scheduled meeting or sooner if material.
checklist.done: every trigger breach has a dated escalation memo and Risk Committee record.

checklist.step: Have the Appointed Actuary review technical assumptions
actions: Review the mortality/morbidity/loss ratio assumptions and reserving basis used across the stressed runs for consistency with the year-end actuarial opinion.
Sign off or note any inconsistency.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary sign-off (or documented exception) is recorded on the technical assumptions.

checklist.step: Compile the stress and scenario testing results register
actions: Log each scenario, its calibration, the resulting capital ratio, trigger status and escalation reference into the results register.
Attach the underlying model run files.
checklist.done: the results register has one complete row per scenario with model files attached.

checklist.step: Feed results into the CISSA and BSCR add-on assessment
actions: Reference the finalized stress-test results in the CISSA's own capital assessment section.
Determine whether any scenario supports a BSCR capital add-on recommendation to the BMA.
Document the recommendation.
checklist.done: the CISSA references the finalized stress results and any BSCR add-on recommendation is documented.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Risk Officer sign-off on the completed testing cycle
actions: Review the full results register and escalation log for completeness.
Sign off the cycle as complete.
Note any scenario deferred and its reason.
checklist.done: the CRO sign-off is recorded on the complete results register with any deferral explained.

checklist.step: File and index the stress-test evidence package
actions: Save the results register, model run files, calibration notes and escalation memos into the compliance evidence repository under the entity and year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the complete stress-test package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and year.

checklist.step: Log any missed scenario or unescalated breach as an exception
actions: Where a mandated scenario was not run or a breach was not escalated on time, open a tracker exception with root cause and remediation owner.
Notify the Board Risk Committee chair.
checklist.done: every missed scenario or late escalation is logged with root cause, owner and committee notification.

checklist.step: Update the scenario library for next cycle
actions: Incorporate any new BMA-mandated scenario or emerging risk identified during the year into next cycle's scenario library.
Retire scenarios no longer material with CRO sign-off.
checklist.done: next cycle's scenario library is updated and CRO-approved.

testing.step: Build the population of scenarios run in the year
actions: Pull the stress-test results register for every entity and scenario run in the test period.
Reconcile the count to the approved workplan.
Resolve any missing scenario before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the approved workplan and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile mandated scenarios to actual runs
actions: Compare the list of BMA-mandated scenarios for the year to the results register.
List any mandated scenario not run as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every mandated scenario is matched to a run or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of scenarios that breached the internal capital trigger.
Take a random sample of at least 5 non-breaching scenarios.
Record the seed and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every trigger-breaching scenario.

testing.step: Re-perform a sampled stressed balance sheet run
actions: Independently rebuild the stressed balance sheet for the sampled scenario using the same base data and documented calibration.
Compare the recomputed post-stress ratio to the register figure.
Treat material differences as exceptions.
testing.done: the recomputed results agree with the register or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify catastrophe scenario inputs
actions: For sampled catastrophe scenarios, confirm the exposure data loaded into the cat model matches the in-force book as of the run date.
Confirm the return-period event selected matches the workplan.
testing.done: the exposure data and event selection are confirmed correct for each sampled catastrophe scenario.

testing.step: Confirm escalation occurred for every trigger breach
actions: For each sampled breaching scenario, confirm an escalation memo exists and a Board Risk Committee record shows it was received.
Flag any breach without escalation.
testing.done: every sampled breach has a confirmed escalation memo and committee record.

testing.step: Verify Appointed Actuary sign-off on assumptions
actions: Obtain the signed technical assumption review from the Appointed Actuary's files for the sampled scenarios.
Confirm date and scope match the results register reference.
testing.done: the Appointed Actuary sign-off is verified as authentic for each sampled scenario.

testing.step: Confirm CISSA/BSCR linkage
actions: Check that the CISSA report and any BSCR add-on recommendation reference the correct finalized results for the sampled scenarios.
Flag any inconsistency in figures between the register and the CISSA.
testing.done: figures in the CISSA and BSCR recommendation agree with the results register for every sampled scenario.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next cycle's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-mandated-scenario threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board Risk Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns identification, computation and quarterly remittance of US Federal Excise Tax (FET) withheld on reinsurance premiums ceded to the Bermuda entity from US-situs risks.

Citation verified against current regula.value: IRC Section 4371 (excise tax on foreign reinsurance) as applied to Bermuda-domiciled reinsurers absent treaty relief, re-read against current IRS guidance and any applicable closing agreement each remittance cycle.

In-scope processes.value: Treaty/facultative premium bordereaux intake, FET applicability determination by cedant and risk location, quarterly tax computation, and IRS Form 720 remittance, across all inward US-risk reinsurance business.

In-scope systems.value: Ceded/assumed premium data sourced from the ERP GL and the ceded accounting platform; FET computation maintained in a dedicated tax workbook.

Compliance procedure documented.value: US Excise Tax (FET) Withholding and Remittance Procedure - bordereaux intake, applicability screen, rate application, Form 720 preparation and remittance.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Tax Director; reviewed annually and on any change to US excise tax regulations or the entity's treaty position.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: IRS Form 720 filed and tax remitted quarterly, by the last day of the month following the end of each calendar quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31).

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tax calendar alerts at Q-end+15/Q-end+25 days to the Tax Manager ahead of each Form 720 due date.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Premium bordereaux, FET computation workpapers, filed Form 720 and remittance confirmations retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late remittance or miscomputed FET is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, interest/penalty exposure and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Director signs off any late-remittance remediation and any voluntary disclosure to the IRS.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All inward US-risk reinsurance premium bordereaux processed in the quarter, per the ceded accounting platform.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a missed Form 720 deadline; FET computation variance beyond $500 or 1% of the quarter's liability (whichever is greater) is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per remittance cycle (quarterly); test performed quarterly over that quarter's population.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the Tax Manager who prepared the FET computation.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly FET test workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the filed Form 720.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed Form 720, premium bordereaux and FET computation workpapers, assembled within 5 business days of an IRS inquiry.

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IRS response; Tax Manager supports with computation detail; Legal Counsel clears any substantive position taken.

checklist.step: Identify all inward US-risk reinsurance premium in the period
actions: Pull the quarter's assumed premium bordereaux from the ceded accounting platform, filtered to cedants and risks with a US situs.
Cross-check against the treaty register to confirm which treaties carry US-risk exposure.
Flag any new treaty not yet assessed for FET applicability.
checklist.done: the quarter's US-risk assumed premium is extracted and reconciled to the treaty register.

checklist.step: Screen each premium line for FET applicability and treaty relief
actions: For each identified line, confirm whether Section 4371 applies (reinsurance of US-situs risk by a foreign insurer) or whether a closing agreement, election, or treaty exemption removes the liability.
Document the applicability determination with citation on a per-treaty basis.
checklist.done: every US-risk premium line has a documented FET applicability determination with citation.

checklist.step: Apply the correct FET rate
actions: Apply the 1% rate to reinsurance premium (or the applicable rate for the specific line of business) per current IRS guidance.
Compute the gross FET liability per treaty and in total for the quarter.
Document the rate source.
checklist.done: FET is computed at the correct rate per treaty with the rate source documented.

checklist.step: Reconcile the computation to the ceded accounting platform premium totals
actions: Tie the FET computation's premium base to the ceded accounting platform's quarterly bordereaux totals.
Investigate and resolve any variance before finalizing the computation.
checklist.done: the FET computation premium base reconciles to the ceded accounting platform with no unresolved variance.

checklist.step: Prepare the IRS Form 720
actions: Complete Form 720 Part II, IRS number 30, with the computed FET liability for the quarter.
Complete Schedule A if required for the entity's deposit obligations.
Have the Tax Analyst independently foot the form against the computation workpaper.
checklist.done: Form 720 is complete and independently footed against the computation workpaper.

checklist.step: Route the completed form for review
actions: Review the FET computation workpaper and completed Form 720 against the treaty register and applicability determinations.
Query any line that looks inconsistent with prior quarters.
Approve for filing once satisfied.
checklist.done: the Tax Director review is documented and the form is approved for filing.

checklist.step: Remit the tax payment
actions: Initiate the EFTPS (Electronic Federal Tax Payment System) payment for the computed FET liability ahead of the due date.
Post the payment in the ERP against the tax liability account.
Retain the EFTPS confirmation number.
checklist.done: the payment is remitted via EFTPS before the due date with a retained confirmation number.

checklist.step: File Form 720 by the statutory deadline
actions: Submit the completed Form 720 by the last day of the month following quarter-end.
Retain the filing confirmation (e-file acknowledgment or certified mail receipt).
Log the filing date on the tax calendar.
checklist.done: Form 720 is filed by the statutory deadline with a retained filing confirmation.

checklist.step: Reconcile the GL tax liability account after remittance
actions: Confirm the tax liability account is cleared by the EFTPS payment amount.
Investigate any residual balance.
Close the quarter's FET accrual in the GL.
checklist.done: the GL tax liability account is reconciled to zero (or a documented residual) after remittance.

checklist.step: Assess any treaty or entity change affecting future FET exposure
actions: Review any new reinsurance treaty, cut-through endorsement, or entity restructuring executed in the quarter for FET impact.
Update the treaty register's FET applicability flags accordingly.
checklist.done: the treaty register's FET flags are current with any quarter's changes reflected.

checklist.step: Log any late payment or filing as an exception
actions: Where a deadline is missed, open a tracker exception recording cause, interest/penalty exposure computed under IRC Section 6651, and a remediation date.
Notify the Tax Director.
checklist.done: any missed deadline is logged with cause, computed exposure and Tax Director notification.

checklist.step: Assess penalty and interest exposure on any late remittance
actions: Compute the failure-to-deposit and failure-to-file penalty and statutory interest using current IRS rates.
Determine whether reasonable-cause abatement applies.
Document the determination.
checklist.done: penalty and interest exposure is computed and an abatement position is documented for any late remittance.

checklist.step: File and index the quarter's FET evidence package
actions: Save the premium bordereaux extract, applicability determinations, computation workpaper, filed Form 720 and EFTPS confirmation into the compliance evidence repository under the entity and quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the complete FET package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity and quarter.

checklist.step: Obtain Tax Director sign-off closing the cycle
actions: Review the completed remittance package and any exceptions raised.
Sign off the quarter as closed.
Note any recurring issue to address in the procedure.
checklist.done: the Tax Director sign-off is recorded and any recurring issue is noted for the procedure update.

checklist.step: Update the FET procedure and treaty register for next cycle
actions: Incorporate any regulatory change, new treaty, or process issue identified during the quarter into the procedure and treaty register ahead of next quarter's cycle.
checklist.done: the procedure and treaty register are updated ahead of the next remittance cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of US-risk premium bordereaux for the quarter
actions: Pull the quarter's assumed premium bordereaux from the ceded accounting platform filtered to US-situs risk.
Reconcile the total to the FET computation workpaper's premium base.
Resolve any variance before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the FET computation workpaper and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filed Form 720
actions: Compare the total FET liability computed from the population to the amount reported on the filed Form 720.
List any variance as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population-derived FET liability agrees with the filed Form 720 or the variance is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of treaties newly assessed for FET applicability in the quarter.
Take a random sample of at least 10 remaining premium lines.
Record the seed and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every newly-assessed treaty.

testing.step: Re-perform the FET applicability determination
actions: Independently assess each sampled treaty's FET applicability against current IRS guidance and the treaty register without referring to the original determination.
Compare conclusions.
Treat any difference as an exception.
testing.done: the independent applicability conclusions agree with the workpaper or differences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Recompute the FET liability on the sample
actions: Independently recompute FET on the sampled premium lines using the applicable rate.
Compare to the workpaper figure.
Treat variances beyond tolerance as exceptions.
testing.done: the recomputed FET agrees with the workpaper within tolerance or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify the EFTPS payment and Form 720 filing
actions: Obtain the EFTPS confirmation and e-file acknowledgment for the quarter.
Confirm the payment date and amount match the computed liability and that both pre-date or meet the statutory deadline.
testing.done: the EFTPS payment and Form 720 filing are verified as timely and matching the computed liability.

testing.step: Confirm GL reconciliation of the tax liability account
actions: Pull the GL tax liability account activity for the quarter.
Confirm it clears to the EFTPS payment amount.
Flag any unreconciled residual.
testing.done: the GL tax liability account is confirmed reconciled or the residual is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test penalty/interest computation on any late item
actions: For any sampled late payment or filing, recompute the penalty and interest under IRC Section 6651 and compare to the amount accrued.
Confirm any abatement position is documented and supportable.
testing.done: the penalty/interest computation and abatement position are verified for every sampled late item.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next quarter's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance-for-late-filing threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report results to the CFO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and CFO reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns annual preparation, issuance and IRS filing of policyholder tax reporting forms (1099-R for US payees, 1042-S for foreign payees) for all reportable annuity and life distributions.

Citation verified against current regula.value: IRC Sections 6047, 3405 and 1441/1461 reporting and withholding requirements as they apply to distributions from the entity's annuity and life business, re-read against the current IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-R and 1042-S each filing season.

In-scope processes.value: Distribution event capture in policy administration, payee tax status determination (US person vs. foreign), withholding calculation, form generation, payee mailing, and IRS/FIRE electronic filing, across all annuity and life policies with a reportable distribution in the year.

In-scope systems.value: Distribution events and payee tax certifications (W-9/W-8BEN) sourced from the policy administration system; forms generated and IRS-filed through the tax reporting workbook and e-file channel.

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policyholder Tax Form Issuance Procedure - distribution extraction, payee tax status validation, withholding computation, form generation, payee mailing and IRS filing.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Tax Manager; reviewed annually and on any IRS form or instruction revision.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 1099-R furnished to payees by January 31 and filed with the IRS by February 28 (paper) / March 31 (electronic); Form 1042-S furnished to payees and filed with the IRS by March 15, with a possible 30-day extension on request.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tax calendar alerts at December 15 (data cut-off), January 15 (form draft complete) and the statutory furnish/file dates, to the Tax Analyst and Tax Manager.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Distribution extract, payee tax status validation, generated forms, mailing confirmation and IRS filing acknowledgment retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed furnish/file deadline, incorrect withholding, or corrected-form issuance is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Manager signs off any corrected-form remediation and any late-filing penalty response.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All annuity and life distribution events in the calendar year that triggered a reportable tax form, per the policy administration system's distribution extract.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a form not furnished/filed by its statutory deadline; withholding computation variance beyond $10 or 0.5% of the distribution (whichever is greater) is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test performed annually over a sample of the year's distribution population.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the Tax Analyst who prepared the forms.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policyholder tax form test workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the IRS filing acknowledgment.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Distribution extract, sampled forms, withholding computations and IRS filing acknowledgment, assembled within 5 business days of an IRS inquiry.

Regulator response path.value: Tax Manager owns the IRS response on policyholder reporting; Annuity Service Specialist supports with policy-level detail.

checklist.step: Extract all reportable distribution events for the calendar year
actions: In the policy administration system run the annual distributions report filtered to surrenders, withdrawals, annuitizations, death benefit payouts and loans deemed distributions.
Export payee name, TIN, policy number, gross distribution, taxable amount and distribution code.
Reconcile the extract row count to the disbursement register in the ERP.
checklist.done: the distribution extract is complete and reconciled to the disbursement register.

checklist.step: Validate payee tax status for each distribution
actions: Pull the on-file W-9 (US persons) or W-8BEN (foreign persons) for each payee from the policy administration system's document repository.
Flag any payee with a missing or expired certification.
For missing certifications apply the default backup withholding or NRA withholding rate per IRS rules.
checklist.done: every distribution has a validated (or defaulted) payee tax status with certification status recorded.

checklist.step: Determine the correct form type per payee
actions: Assign Form 1099-R to distributions to validated US persons.
Assign Form 1042-S to distributions to foreign payees or payees defaulted to NRA withholding.
Document the assignment logic applied to each row.
checklist.done: every distribution row is assigned the correct form type with the assignment logic documented.

checklist.step: Compute federal (and where applicable state) withholding
actions: Apply the default 10% federal withholding on periodic/nonperiodic annuity distributions absent a payee election, or the payee's elected rate on file.
Apply the 30% NRA withholding rate on Form 1042-S distributions unless a treaty rate is properly claimed on a valid W-8BEN.
Recompute and cross-check a sample of the withholding calculations.
checklist.done: withholding is computed for every distribution with the applicable rate documented and cross-checked.

checklist.step: Apply treaty rate reductions where properly claimed
actions: For foreign payees claiming a reduced treaty withholding rate, confirm the W-8BEN cites a valid treaty article and the payee's country has an in-force US tax treaty.
Apply the reduced rate only where the claim is fully substantiated.
Document any claim rejected for insufficient substantiation.
checklist.done: every treaty rate reduction applied is substantiated by a valid, on-file claim.

checklist.step: Generate draft forms
actions: Populate Form 1099-R and Form 1042-S templates from the validated distribution and withholding data.
Run a system-generated total that ties gross distributions and withholding to the ERP general ledger tax withholding accrual.
Correct any discrepancy before proceeding.
checklist.done: draft forms are generated and their totals tie to the ERP withholding accrual.

checklist.step: Route drafts for independent review
actions: Sample a cross-section of draft forms across distribution types and payee tax statuses.
Recompute the withholding and confirm the form type assignment independently.
Return any error for correction.
checklist.done: sampled draft forms are independently recomputed with no unresolved errors before finalization.

checklist.step: Finalize and print/electronically deliver payee copies
actions: Finalize the form set once review is complete.
Mail paper copies (or deliver electronically to payees who consented) to the address/contact on file in the policy administration system.
Log the mailing/delivery date per payee.
checklist.done: every payee copy is mailed or electronically delivered with the delivery date logged.

checklist.step: Confirm payee copies are furnished by the statutory deadline
actions: Confirm 1099-R copies were furnished by January 31 and 1042-S copies by March 15.
For any payee copy not confirmed delivered, trigger a re-mail before the deadline.
checklist.done: all payee copies are confirmed furnished on or before their statutory deadline.

checklist.step: File the forms with the IRS electronically
actions: Transmit Form 1099-R data through the IRS FIRE (Filing Information Returns Electronically) system and Form 1042-S data per IRS e-file specifications.
Retain the transmission acceptance confirmation for each form set.
checklist.done: IRS transmission acceptance confirmations are on file for both form sets.

checklist.step: Reconcile total forms filed to the distribution population
actions: Compare the count and dollar total of forms filed to the original distribution extract and the GL withholding accrual.
Investigate and resolve any variance.
checklist.done: filed form totals reconcile to the distribution extract and GL accrual with no unresolved variance.

checklist.step: Handle corrected forms
actions: Where a payee reports an error or a data correction is identified after filing, prepare a corrected Form 1099-R/1042-S per IRS correction procedures.
Re-issue to the payee and re-file with the IRS.
Log the correction reason.
checklist.done: every identified error has a corrected form issued to the payee and re-filed with the IRS, with the reason logged.

checklist.step: Log any missed deadline or incorrect withholding as an exception
actions: Open a tracker exception for any form not furnished/filed by deadline or any material withholding error.
Record root cause and remediation date.
Notify the Controller of any GL correction needed.
checklist.done: every missed deadline or withholding error is logged with root cause, remediation date and Controller notification.

checklist.step: File and index the year's evidence package
actions: Save the distribution extract, tax status validations, withholding computations, final forms, mailing log and IRS acceptance confirmations into the compliance evidence repository under the tax year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the complete policyholder tax form package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by tax year.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with Tax Manager sign-off and update the procedure
actions: Review the completed filing package and any exceptions.
Sign off the cycle as closed.
Update the procedure with any process or system issue identified for next year.
checklist.done: the Tax Manager sign-off is recorded and the procedure is updated ahead of next year's cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of reportable distributions for the year
actions: Pull the distribution extract from the policy administration system for the calendar year.
Reconcile the count and dollar total to the ERP disbursement register.
Resolve discrepancies before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the disbursement register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to forms filed
actions: Match the distribution population to the filed 1099-R/1042-S count.
List any distribution with no matching form as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population distribution is matched to a filed form or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of Form 1042-S (foreign payee) distributions.
Take a random sample of at least 25 Form 1099-R distributions.
Record the seed and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every 1042-S distribution.

testing.step: Re-verify payee tax status and treaty claims
actions: Independently pull the W-9/W-8BEN on file for each sampled payee.
Confirm the tax status and any treaty claim used matches what was applied on the form.
Treat mismatches as exceptions.
testing.done: payee tax status and treaty claims are independently confirmed for every sampled form.

testing.step: Recompute withholding on the sample
actions: Independently recompute federal or NRA withholding for each sampled distribution using the applicable rate.
Compare to the amount reported on the form.
Treat variances beyond tolerance as exceptions.
testing.done: the recomputed withholding agrees with the filed form within tolerance or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify payee delivery timing
actions: Pull the mailing/delivery log for each sampled payee.
Confirm the delivery date is on or before the statutory furnish deadline (January 31 for 1099-R, March 15 for 1042-S).
testing.done: delivery timing is confirmed compliant for every sampled payee or the exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify IRS filing acceptance for the sample
actions: Pull the FIRE system (or 1042-S e-file) acceptance record for each sampled form.
Confirm the transmission date is on or before the statutory filing deadline and the record shows Accepted status.
testing.done: IRS acceptance is confirmed for every sampled form, filed on time.

testing.step: Test correction handling
actions: For any sampled form later corrected, confirm the corrected form was issued to the payee and re-filed with the IRS, and the correction reason is documented.
testing.done: correction handling is verified complete for every sampled corrected form.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance-for-missed-deadline threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report results to the CFO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and CFO reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns entity-level FATCA and CRS classification, due diligence and annual information return filing with the IRS (Form 8966 via IDES) and the Bermuda tax authority's CRS portal.

Citation verified against current regula.value: US FATCA (IRC Sections 1471-1474) and the Bermuda International Cooperation (Tax Information Exchange Agreements) Act 2005 / Common Reporting Standard regulations, re-read against current IRS FATCA and Bermuda CRS filing guidance each cycle.

In-scope processes.value: FATCA/CRS entity classification review, policyholder/counterparty due diligence and self-certification collection, reportable account identification, Form 8966 and CRS return preparation, and IRS IDES and Bermuda portal submission, across all reportable financial accounts (annuity and cash-value life policies).

In-scope systems.value: Reportable account data sourced from policy administration and the ERP; self-certifications stored in the document management repository; FATCA/CRS returns prepared in the tax reporting workbook.

Compliance procedure documented.value: FATCA/CRS Classification, Due Diligence and Reporting Procedure - entity classification, account due diligence, reportable account identification, return preparation and dual-channel submission.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Tax Director; reviewed annually and on any change to FATCA/CRS regulations or the entity's registration status.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 8966 filed with the IRS via IDES by March 31 following the reporting calendar year; Bermuda CRS return filed with the Ministry of Finance by May 31 following the reporting year.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tax calendar alerts at January 31 (due diligence cut-off), February 28 (draft return complete) and the statutory filing dates, to the Tax Director and Tax Manager.

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Entity classification memo, self-certifications, reportable account list, filed Form 8966/CRS return and submission acknowledgments retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any missed filing deadline, misclassified account or missing self-certification is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date.

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Tax Director signs off any remediation, including any late-filing notice response to the IRS or Bermuda Ministry of Finance.

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All financial accounts (annuity and cash-value life policies) open at year-end, per the account population used for the FATCA/CRS due diligence review.

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for a missed filing deadline; any reportable account omitted from the filed return is a fail.

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; test performed annually over a sample of the account population and 100% of accounts flagged reportable.

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer independent of the Tax Manager who performed the due diligence and prepared the returns.

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual FATCA/CRS test workpaper stored in the compliance evidence repository, cross-referenced to the IRS IDES and Bermuda portal submission acknowledgments.

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Entity classification memo, due diligence file, filed Form 8966/CRS return and submission acknowledgments, assembled within 5 business days of an IRS or Ministry of Finance inquiry.

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns the IRS/Bermuda Ministry of Finance response; Legal Counsel clears any substantive position on account classification.

checklist.step: Confirm the entity's FATCA and CRS classification
actions: Review the entity's FATCA classification (Foreign Financial Institution status, GIIN registration) and CRS classification (Reporting Financial Institution) against current IRS and Bermuda guidance.
Confirm the entity's GIIN is active on the IRS FFI list.
Document the classification rationale.
checklist.done: the FATCA and CRS classification is documented and the GIIN is confirmed active.

checklist.step: Extract the population of financial accounts subject to due diligence
actions: Pull all annuity and cash-value life policies in force at year-end from policy administration.
Export policyholder name, address, TIN/country of tax residence and account value.
Reconcile the extract to the in-force policy count in the ERP.
checklist.done: the account population is extracted and reconciled to the in-force policy count.

checklist.step: Apply indicia search and collect self-certifications
actions: Run the electronic indicia search (non-domestic address, non-domestic phone, standing instructions to a foreign account, power of attorney to a foreign address) against each account.
For accounts with indicia or above the reporting threshold, request a self-certification (W-9, W-8BEN, or CRS self-certification form) if not already on file.
checklist.done: every in-scope account has an indicia search result and a current self-certification or a documented follow-up in progress.

checklist.step: Classify each account as reportable or not
actions: Apply the FATCA reportable-account test (US indicia, no valid documentation curing it) and the CRS reportable-account test (tax residence in a CRS participating jurisdiction) to each account.
Document the classification and the evidence relied on.
checklist.done: every account has a documented reportable/non-reportable classification with supporting evidence.

checklist.step: Compile the reportable account list
actions: Extract all accounts classified reportable under FATCA into one list and all accounts reportable under CRS (by jurisdiction) into another.
Include account balance/value and any reportable payments made during the year.
Cross-check for accounts reportable under both regimes.
checklist.done: the FATCA and CRS reportable account lists are compiled with balances, payments and cross-regime accounts flagged.

checklist.step: Prepare Form 8966 (FATCA)
actions: Populate Form 8966 for each FATCA-reportable account with account holder identifying information, account number, balance and payment data per IRS instructions.
Foot the form totals against the reportable account list.
checklist.done: Form 8966 is complete and its totals tie to the reportable account list.

checklist.step: Prepare the Bermuda CRS return
actions: Populate the CRS return per the Bermuda Ministry of Finance's prescribed XML schema, organized by each reportable jurisdiction.
Foot the return totals against the CRS reportable account list.
checklist.done: the CRS return is complete, schema-valid and its totals tie to the reportable account list.

checklist.step: Route both returns for independent technical review
actions: Review the classification rationale, reportable account lists and both draft returns for consistency with the entity's FATCA/CRS classification.
Query any account classification that appears inconsistent.
Approve for filing once resolved.
checklist.done: the Tax Director review is documented and both returns are approved for filing.

checklist.step: Register or confirm access to the IRS IDES and Bermuda CRS filing channels
actions: Confirm the entity's IDES account credentials and encryption certificate are current for FATCA transmission.
Confirm portal access credentials for the Bermuda Ministry of Finance's CRS filing system are current.
Renew any expiring credential ahead of the filing window.
checklist.done: IDES and Bermuda CRS portal access are confirmed current before the filing window opens.

checklist.step: Transmit Form 8966 through IDES
actions: Package the Form 8966 XML file per IRS FATCA XML schema, encrypt per IDES requirements and transmit through the IDES portal by March 31.
Retain the transmission receipt and status notification.
checklist.done: Form 8966 is transmitted through IDES by the deadline with a retained receipt and accepted status.

checklist.step: Submit the CRS return to the Bermuda Ministry of Finance
actions: Upload the CRS XML return through the Ministry of Finance's CRS filing portal by May 31.
Retain the portal's submission confirmation.
checklist.done: the CRS return is submitted through the Bermuda portal by the deadline with a retained confirmation.

checklist.step: Reconcile submitted totals to the reportable account lists post-filing
actions: Compare the account count and balance/payment totals on the transmitted returns to the original reportable account lists.
Investigate and resolve any discrepancy.
Document the reconciliation.
checklist.done: submitted return totals reconcile to the reportable account lists with no unresolved discrepancy.

checklist.step: Log any missed deadline, rejected transmission or misclassification as an exception
actions: Open a tracker exception for any IDES/CRS rejection, missed deadline or account later found misclassified.
Record root cause and remediation date.
Re-transmit corrected data where required.
checklist.done: every rejection, missed deadline or misclassification is logged with root cause, remediation date and any required re-transmission completed.

checklist.step: File and index the year's FATCA/CRS evidence package
actions: Save the classification memo, indicia search results, self-certifications, reportable account lists, filed Form 8966/CRS return and transmission acknowledgments into the compliance evidence repository under the tax year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: the complete FATCA/CRS package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by tax year.

checklist.step: Close the cycle with Tax Director sign-off and update the procedure
actions: Review the completed filing package and any exceptions.
Sign off the cycle as closed.
Update the classification and due diligence procedure with any regulatory or process change identified for next year.
checklist.done: the Tax Director sign-off is recorded and the procedure is updated ahead of next year's cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of financial accounts subject to FATCA/CRS review
actions: Pull the year-end in-force policy extract used for due diligence.
Reconcile the count to the ERP in-force policy count.
Resolve discrepancies before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the ERP in-force count and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile reportable account lists to the filed returns
actions: Compare the FATCA and CRS reportable account lists to the accounts actually reported on the filed Form 8966 and CRS return.
List any omitted or extra account as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the reportable account lists reconcile to the filed returns or discrepancies are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of accounts classified reportable under either regime.
Take a random sample of at least 25 accounts classified non-reportable.
Record the seed and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every reportable account.

testing.step: Re-perform the indicia search and classification
actions: Independently re-run the indicia search and reportable-account test on each sampled account using the account data as of the review date.
Compare the conclusion to the original classification.
Treat differences as exceptions.
testing.done: the independent classification agrees with the original for every sampled account or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify self-certifications on file
actions: For each sampled account, confirm a valid, dated self-certification (or documented follow-up) exists in the document management repository.
Confirm the country of tax residence on the certification matches the classification used.
testing.done: a valid self-certification (or documented follow-up) is confirmed for every sampled account.

testing.step: Recompute reported balances and payments
actions: Independently pull the account balance and any reportable payment for sampled reportable accounts from policy administration.
Compare to the amount reported on Form 8966/the CRS return.
Treat variances beyond tolerance as exceptions.
testing.done: the recomputed balances/payments agree with the filed return within tolerance or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify IDES and Bermuda portal transmission
actions: Pull the IDES transmission receipt and status, and the Bermuda Ministry of Finance's submission confirmation.
Confirm both transmissions occurred on or before their statutory deadlines and show accepted status.
testing.done: both transmissions are confirmed accepted and on time.

testing.step: Confirm GIIN and registration currency
actions: Check the entity's GIIN against the current IRS FFI list.
Confirm the Bermuda CRS registration is active as of the filing date.
testing.done: the GIIN and Bermuda CRS registration are confirmed active as of the filing date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each exception found.
Assign root cause and owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: every exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance-for-omitted-reportable-account threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have an independent reviewer sign the workpaper.
Report results to the CFO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and CFO reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
